key_insight: A weakly supervised deep learning model (MIMIC) can triage early-stage mycosis fungoides on whole-slide images and help separate it from benign inflammatory dermatoses with high sensitivity.
clinical_relevance: As a screening aid, it could reduce unnecessary ancillary testing and pathologist workload while preserving near-complete detection of classic MF cases.
method: Trained with attention-based multiple-instance learning on 3,339 WSIs from two Dutch centers using expert-panel consensus labels.
Externally validated on 371 WSIs from four independent European centers.
Compared against 11 (dermato-)pathologists in a blinded reader study and then tested in a held-out consecutive clinical cohort.
evidence_signal: The updated model achieved AUROC 0.87 in the held-out cohort, with 97.8% sensitivity and 50.2% specificity at the prespecified 0.04 threshold.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated in a retrospective, mainly histology-based workflow, so prospective real-world impact and generalizability across broader biopsy populations still need confirmation.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
